I think the disagreement is now really about what we mean by “per-exposure” and about marginal versus conditional hazard, not about the algebra.

The algebra everyone is writing down is correct. With p completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated

S_v(t)=p+(1-p)S_0(t),   h_v(t)=λ0 (1-p)S0(t)/[p+(1-p)S0(t)],   h_u(t)=λ0

so the hazard conditional on remaining uninfected up to time t,

HR_cond(t)=h_v(t)/h_u(t)=(1-p)S0(t)/[p+(1-p)S0(t)]≤1-p,

declines from HR_cond(0)=1-p to 0. That is the hazard in the still-at-risk risk set. It declines because the 1-p susceptible fraction is selectively depleted by infection while the p protected fraction stays in the denominator. That is a selection/enrichment phenomenon in the risk set, not a change in the biological per-exposure risk of an individual who remains susceptible.

The incidence rate ratio that is used in practice is a marginal population quantity: total events divided by total person-time accrued by the whole vaccinated cohort, protected person-time included. On a per person-time basis the vaccinated cohort is a mixture

λ_V = p·0 + (1-p)·λ_0 = (1-p)λ_0

with the same exposure intensity in the two arms. Hence with constant exposure

IR_V = exposure × E[r|v] = exposure ×[p·0+(1-p)r_0] = (1-p)IR_U

and

IRR = IR_V/IR_U =1-p,   1-IRR =p.

That p is the average reduction in risk per exposure in the vaccinated population: average per-exposure risk vaccinated = (1-p) × risk per exposure unvaccinated, so the average per-exposure risk ratio is 1-p and the average per-exposure VE is 1-(1-p)=p.

The declining conditional HR(t) is exactly why the cumulative risk ratio stays constant, F_v(T)=(1-p)F_0(T), RR_cum(T)=1-p, 1-RR_cum=p. The “immortal person-time” that the A camp points to is the p person-time with zero events. Counting it is not a bias for a population-average rate; it is the correct denominator for the average rate per vaccinated person, i.e. the average per-exposure risk averaged over responders and non-responders.

In other words, 1-HR(0)=p is the population-average instantaneous per-exposure reduction at time zero, and under constant exposure the marginal incidence density ratio recovers that same p. The time-averaged 1-IRR is >p only if we redefine per-exposure VE as the instantaneous conditional hazard among survivors, 1-HR(t), and then compare it to a finite-follow-up average hazard. With the conventional epidemiologic definition of per-exposure VE as the average reduction in probability of infection per unit exposure across the vaccinated population, the rate ratio is constant and 1-IRR = p correctly estimates the population-average per-exposure efficacy. The responder-specific 100% protection is a conditional biological effect in the p sub-cohort; the marginal 1-IRR = p is the population average of that effect, which is the quantity normally reported as VE_IRR for an all-or-nothing vaccine.

7.text:
A. overestimate

For a pure all-or-nothing / proportion protected mechanism let p be the fraction completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated with a constant unvaccinated force of infection λ0.

$S_{u}(t)=\exp[-\lambda_{0}t]$,
$S_{v}(t)=p+(1-p)S_{u}(t)$

$h_{u}(t)=\lambda_{0}$
$h_{v}(t)=-\frac{d}{dt}\log S_{v}(t)=\lambda_{0}\dfrac{(1-p)S_{u}(t)}{p+(1-p)S_{u}(t)}$

$HR(t)=\dfrac{h_{v}}{h_{u}}=\dfrac{(1-p)S_{u}(t)}{p+(1-p)S_{u}(t)}\le1-p$
$HR(0)=1-p$, $HR(t)\downarrow0$.

Instantaneous per-exposure / proportion protected efficacy
$VE_{e}=1-HR(0)=p$
and $F_{v}(T)=(1-p)F_{u}(T)$, $RR_{cum}(T)=1-p$, $1-RR_{cum}=p$.

The incidence density used for IRR is cases / total person-time

$E_{v}(T)=N(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]$
$PT_{v}(T)=NpT+(1-p)N\int_{0}^{T}S_{u}(s)ds$

$IR_{v}(T)=\dfrac{(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}{pT+(1-p)\int_{0}^{T}S_{u}(s)ds}$,
$IR_{u}=\lambda_{0}$,

$IRR(T)=\dfrac{(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}{p\lambda_{0}T+(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}<1-p$ for $T>0$
$1-IRR(T)=\dfrac{p\lambda_{0}T}{p\lambda_{0}T+(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}>p$.

$1-IRR(T)\to p$ as $T\to0$ and $1-IRR(T)\to1$ as $T\to\infty$.

The p completely immune fraction contributes event-free immortal person-time for the whole follow-up while the $1-p$ susceptible fraction is progressively depleted by infection. The time-averaged hazard is therefore $<HR(0)=1-p$ and the finite-follow-up $1-IRR$ is a person-time diluted upwardly biased proxy for the instantaneous per-exposure reduction $p=1-HR(0)$. The bias grows with follow-up and attack rate.

The unbiased estimator of the all-or-nothing proportion protected is the cumulative risk ratio $1-RR_{cum}=p$. For a leaky vaccine $HR(t)$ is constant and $1-IRR=VE_{e}$.

Remark on definitions. On the population-average marginal hazard scale $\lambda_{V}=p\cdot0+(1-p)\lambda_{0}$ the $T\to0$ limit gives $1-IRR=p$, which is the average reduction per unit calendar time across the whole cohort. The responder-conditional biological per-exposure effect is 100% in the p sub-cohort and 0% in the $1-p$ sub-cohort, so $p$ is the population average of those extremes. Under the conventional finite follow-up epidemiologic definition $VE_{e}=1-HR(0)=p$, the observable $1-IRR(T)$ overestimates it for any realistic $T>0$.

E[r | vaccinated] = p·0 + (1-p)·r0 = (1-p)r0

so on the population-average scale

RRpe = E[r|v]/r0 =1-p

VEpe =1-RRpe =p.

Incidence rate = exposure rate × average per-exposure risk, so on the marginal level

λV = p·0 + (1-p)λ0 = (1-p)λ0
λU = λ0

IRR = λV/λU =1-p
1-IRR =p

is constant in time for an all-or-nothing vaccine under constant exposure. That p is the average reduction in Pr[infection|exposure] across the vaccinated population, which is the usual epidemiologic definition of per-exposure vaccine efficacy.

Counting the person-time of the p protected fraction in the denominator is not immortal-person-time bias for a marginal rate; it is the correct denominator for the average rate per vaccinated person. The protected person-time is precisely how the average events per calendar time are reduced to (1-p) of the unvaccinated level. The fact that the cumulative risk ratio is also Fv(T)=(1-p)Fu(T), RRcum(T)=1-p, 1-RRcum=p shows the marginal rate and marginal cumulative risk are coherent.

The 1-IRR(T)>p calculation that is quoted for finite follow-up is the time-averaged conditional hazard compared to the instantaneous conditional hazard at time zero, 1-HR(0)=p. That is a comparison of a conditional-on-survival quantity HR(t) with an integrated average hazard. The instantaneous conditional HR(0)=1-p is the per-contact reduction at the moment of first exposure. The marginal rate ratio 1-p is the population-average reduction per exposure averaged over responders and non-responders. The responder-specific 100% block in the p sub-cohort is a conditional biological effect; the marginal 1-IRR=p is the population average of 100% in the p fraction and 0% in the 1-p fraction, which is the quantity normally reported as VEIRR for an all-or-nothing vaccine.

On the conventional population-average definition of per-exposure VE, the rate ratio is constant and 1-IRR correctly estimates the average per-exposure efficacy p.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. underestimate

I think the algebra everyone has written down is essentially correct and the disagreement is really definitional. With p completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated

S_v(t)=p+(1-p)S0(t),   h_v(t)=λ0 (1-p)S0(t)/[p+(1-p)S0(t)],   h_u(t)=λ0

HR(t)=(1-p)S0(t)/[p+(1-p)S0(t)]≤1-p, HR(0)=1-p and HR(t)→0.

The finite follow-up incidence density is

IR_v(T)=(1-p)[1-S0(T)]/[pT+(1-p)∫0^T S0(s)ds]

so that IRR(T)<1-p and 1-IRR(T)=pλ0T/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-S0(T)]]>p, with 1-IRR(T)→1 as T→∞. The p fraction contributes event-free immortal person-time and the 1-p susceptible fraction is progressively depleted, so the time-averaged 1-IRR does overstate the population-average proportion protected p=1-RR_cum and 1-HR(0). Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 are right on that point.

The issue is what “per-exposure vaccine efficacy” means. Mechanistically per-exposure efficacy is the reduction in Pr[infection|exposure] for a host in whom the vaccine can act. In an all-or-nothing mechanism that is binary:

* responder, fraction p: per-exposure risk =0, per-exposure VE = 1 - 0/r0 =100%
* non-responder, fraction 1-p: per-exposure risk =r0, per-exposure VE =0%

The marginal incidence density that enters an IRR is the mixture λ_V = p·0 + (1-p)λ0 = (1-p)λ_U, so IRR =1-p and 1-IRR =p. 1-IRR is therefore the population-average of the two extremes p×100% + (1-p)×0%. It is the average reduction in incidence per person-time and the fraction of vaccinees made immune, not the biological per-exposure reduction realized when the vaccine does act.

As Colleague 1 notes in his own remark, and as Colleague 3 repeats, in responder-specific language 1-IRR is an underestimate of the 100% biological per-exposure effect in the p sub-cohort, with p being the fraction of individuals who experience that 100% effect rather than the per-exposure reduction itself. The declining conditional hazard h_v(t) is depletion of the at-risk pool, not a change in per-exposure susceptibility for anyone who remains susceptible. Conditional on being susceptible the per-exposure risk stays r0, conditional on being protected it stays 0.

Hence relative to the responder-conditional, per-contact biological effect the marginal 1-IRR =p is a conservative, diluted summary. The population-average rate ratio is the correct average reduction per person-time, but it is downward biased for the true biological per-exposure protection conferred in responders. That is the usual underestimate reading.

6.text:
A. overestimate

With a pure all-or-nothing mechanism let p be the fraction completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated with constant force of infection λ0.

$S_{u}(t)=e^{-\lambda_{0}t}$, $S_{v}(t)=p+(1-p)S_{u}(t)$

$h_{u}=\lambda_{0}$,
$h_{v}(t)=-\frac{d}{dt}\log S_{v}= \lambda_{0}\frac{(1-p)S_{u}(t)}{p+(1-p)S_{u}(t)}$

$HR(t)=h_{v}/h_{u}= \frac{(1-p)S_{u}(t)}{p+(1-p)S_{u}(t)}\le 1-p$,
$HR(0)=1-p$, $HR(t)\downarrow0$.

The instantaneous per-exposure / proportion protected efficacy is
$VE_{e}=1-HR(0)=p$ and the cumulative risk is proportional
$F_{v}(T)=(1-p)F_{u}(T)$, $RR_{cum}(T)=1-p$, $1-RR_{cum}=p$.

The incidence density used in practice is cases per total person-time

$E_{v}(T)=N(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]$,
$PT_{v}(T)=NpT+(1-p)N\int_{0}^{T}S_{u}(s)ds$,

$IR_{v}(T)=\frac{(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}{pT+(1-p)\int_{0}^{T}S_{u}(s)ds}$,
$IR_{u}=\lambda_{0}$.

Hence for constant λ0

$IRR(T)=\frac{(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}{p\lambda_{0}T+(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}<1-p$, $T>0$

$1-IRR(T)=\frac{p\lambda_{0}T}{p\lambda_{0}T+(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}>p=1-HR(0)$,

$1-IRR(T)\to p$ as $T\to0$ and $1-IRR(T)\to1$ as $T\to\infty$.

The p fraction contributes event-free immortal person-time for the whole follow-up while the 1-p susceptible fraction is progressively depleted by infection. The time-averaged hazard is therefore $<HR(0)=1-p$ and the finite-follow-up $1-IRR$ is a person-time diluted, upwardly biased proxy for the instantaneous per-exposure reduction $p=1-HR(0)$. The bias grows with follow-up and attack rate and vanishes only as $T\to0$.

The unbiased estimator of the all-or-nothing proportion protected is the cumulative risk ratio $1-RR_{cum}=p$. For a leaky vaccine $HR(t)$ is constant and $1-IRR=VE_{e}$. On the population-average marginal hazard scale $\lambda_{V}=(1-p)\lambda_{0}$ the limit is $1-IRR=p$, and the responder-specific 100% biological effect in the $p$ sub-cohort is diluted to $p$ on the marginal scale. Under the conventional finite follow-up definition $VE_{e}=1-HR(0)=p$, the observable $1-IRR(T)$ overestimates it.

I think the core of the disagreement is marginal versus conditional, and once that is made explicit the incidence rate ratio is doing exactly what it is designed to do.

Let r0 be per-exposure infection risk in an unvaccinated susceptible and let exposure intensity be the same in the two arms. In an all-or-nothing vaccine a fraction p is made biologically non-susceptible and 1-p is phenotypically identical to unvaccinated. The average per-exposure risk in the vaccinated cohort is the mixture

E[r|v] = p·0 + (1-p)·r0 = (1-p) r0

so on the population average scale

RR_pe = E[r|v]/r0 = 1-p ,   VE_pe = 1-RR_pe = p

With constant exposure intensity incidence rate = exposure rate × per-exposure risk, so the marginal rate for the whole vaccinated cohort is

λV = p·0 + (1-p)·λ0 = (1-p) λ0 ,   λU = λ0

IRR = λV/λU = 1-p ,   1-IRR = p

constant in time. That p is the average reduction in risk per exposure across the vaccinated population, which is the standard epidemiologic definition of per-exposure VE used with rate studies.

hV(t)= λ0 (1-p)Su(t)/[p+(1-p)Su(t)] is the hazard conditional on remaining uninfected up to t. It declines because the 1-p susceptible stratum is progressively depleted by infection while the p protected stratum stays in the risk set and continues to contribute event-free person-time. That is risk-set enrichment / selection, not a change in the biological per-exposure susceptibility of an individual who remains susceptible. Conditional on being susceptible the per-exposure risk stays r0, conditional on being protected it stays 0.

Counting the person-time contributed by the p protected fraction in the denominator of the incidence rate is not immortal person-time bias for the marginal rate; it is the correct denominator for the average rate per vaccinated person. The protected person-time is precisely how the average events per calendar time are reduced to (1-p) times the unvaccinated rate. The cumulative risk ratio is coherent with this, Fv(T) = (1-p)Fu(T), so 1-RR(T)=p.

The 1-IRR(T) > p calculation is a comparison of a finite follow-up time-averaged conditional hazard with the instantaneous conditional hazard HR(0). The observable IRR targets the marginal incidence density, i.e. total events over total person-time accrued by the whole cohort. On the conventional population-average definition of per-exposure efficacy that marginal rate ratio estimates the average per-exposure reduction without bias for an all-or-nothing vaccine, and 1-IRR = p correctly recovers the average per-exposure VE. The responder-specific 100% effect is a conditional biological effect in the p sub-cohort; the marginal 1-IRR = p is the population average of 100% in the p fraction and 0% in the 1-p fraction, which is the quantity normally reported as VE_IRR.

The algebra everyone has written for the all-or-nothing model is correct, the disagreement is where the estimand lives.

$S_{v}(t)=p+(1-p)S_{0}(t)$ gives the conditional hazard among those still uninfected

$h_{v}(t)= \lambda_{0}\frac{(1-p)S_{0}(t)}{p+(1-p)S_{0}(t)}$,

which declines from $1-p$ to 0. That decline is risk-set enrichment: the $1-p$ phenotypically unvaccinated fraction is progressively depleted by infection while the $p$ completely protected fraction stays in the denominator and keeps contributing event-free person-time. It is a selection effect in the survivors, not a change in the biological per-exposure susceptibility of an individual who remains susceptible. Conditional on being susceptible the per-exposure risk stays $r_{0}$, conditional on being protected it stays $0$.

An incidence rate ratio is a marginal population quantity: total events divided by total person-time accrued by the whole vaccinated cohort, protected person-time included. On a per-exposure basis with constant exposure intensity

$E[r\mid v]=p\cdot0+(1-p)r_{0}=(1-p)r_{0}$

so the average per-exposure risk ratio is $1-p$ and the average per-exposure VE is

$VE_{pe}=1-(1-p)=p$.

$\lambda_{V}=p\cdot0+(1-p)\lambda_{0}=(1-p)\lambda_{0}$,
$\lambda_{U}=\lambda_{0}$

$IRR=\lambda_{V}/\lambda_{U}=1-p$, $1-IRR=p$,

constant in time. That $p$ is the average reduction in risk per exposure across the vaccinated cohort, which is the usual epidemiologic definition of per-exposure VE used in rate studies.

The protected person-time is exactly how the average events per calendar time are reduced to $(1-p)$ of the unvaccinated rate. 2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. underestimate

I agree with the algebra that is now on the table and I think we can all accept the time-averaging facts.

With p completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated, S_v(t)=p+(1-p)S_0(t)
h_v(t)=λ0 (1-p)S_0(t)/[p+(1-p)S_0(t)], h_u=λ0
HR(t)=(1-p)S_0(t)/[p+(1-p)S_0(t)] ≤1-p, HR(0)=1-p, HR(t)↓0.

E_v(T)=N(1-p)[1-S_0(T)], PT_v(T)=NpT+(1-p)N∫0^T S_0(s)ds
so that
IRR(T)=(1-p)[1-S_0(T)]/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-S_0(T)]]<1-p
and 1-IRR(T)=pλ0T/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-S_0(T)]]>p, →1 as T→∞.
The p fraction does contribute event-free person-time and the 1-p susceptible fraction is progressively depleted. That is correct for the calendar-time marginal rate.

The disagreement is definitional: what is “per-exposure vaccine efficacy”.

Mechanistically per-exposure efficacy is the reduction in Pr[infection|exposure] for a host in whom the vaccine can act. In an all-or-nothing mechanism that is binary and time-invariant conditional on stratum:

* responder, fraction p: per-exposure risk =0, per-exposure VE =1-0/r0 =100%
* non-responder, fraction 1-p: per-exposure risk =r0, per-exposure VE =0%

h_v(t) declines not because per-exposure susceptibility changes for an individual who remains susceptible, but because the risk set is enriched by the p protected who stay in the denominator and the 1-p susceptible are selectively removed by infection. Conditional on remaining susceptible the per-exposure risk stays r0, conditional on being protected it stays 0.

The marginal incidence density that enters an IRR is the mixture
λ_V = p·0 + (1-p)λ0 = (1-p)λ_U
so IRR=1-p and 1-IRR=p. That p is the average reduction in incidence per person-time across the whole vaccinated cohort, which is also the proportion of individuals made immune, 1-RR_cum.

It is not the biological per-exposure reduction realized when the vaccine does act. The marginal 1-IRR=p averages the 100% block in responders with the 0% effect in the 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated fraction and is therefore diluted downwards relative to the 100% per-contact protection seen in responders.

As Colleague 1 notes in his own remark, and Colleague 3 repeats, in responder-specific language 1-IRR is an underestimate of the 100% biological per-exposure effect, with p being the fraction of individuals who experience that effect rather than the per-exposure reduction itself. The population-average value p is the correct average reduction across the cohort, but it is a conservative, downward-biased summary of the true per-exposure protection conferred by the vaccine in those who respond.

Hence relative to the responder-conditional, per-contact biological definition of per-exposure efficacy, the observable 1-IRR is a diluted average and underestimates the biological per-exposure block that occurs in the p sub-cohort.

1.text:
A. overestimate

With a pure all-or-nothing / proportion protected model let p be the fraction
completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated with unvaccinated
force of infection λ0.

$S_u(t)=e^{-\lambda_0 t}$, $S_v(t)=p+(1-p)S_u(t)$

$h_u(t)=\lambda_0$
$h_v(t)=-\frac{d}{dt}\log S_v(t)=\lambda_0\frac{(1-p)S_u(t)}{p+(1-p)S_u(t)}$

$HR(t)=\frac{h_v}{h_u}= \frac{(1-p)S_u(t)}{p+(1-p)S_u(t)}\le 1-p$
$HR(0)=1-p$, $HR(t)\downarrow0$.

Instantaneous per-exposure / proportion protected efficacy

$VE_e =1-HR(0)=p$

and on the cumulative scale

$F_v(T)=(1-p)F_u(T)$, $RR_{cum}(T)=1-p$, $1-RR_{cum}=p$.

The incidence density actually used for an IRR is cases / total person-time.

$E_v(T)=N(1-p)[1-S_u(T)]$
$PT_v(T)=NpT+(1-p)N\int_0^T S_u(s)ds$

$IR_v(T)=\frac{(1-p)[1-S_u(T)]}{pT+(1-p)\int_0^T S_u(s)ds}$, $IR_u=\lambda_0$

The vector of disagreement is entirely definitional: what we mean by “per-exposure vaccine efficacy” in an all-or-nothing model.

Let r0 be the per-exposure infection risk in an unvaccinated susceptible host and let exposure intensity be constant in the two arms. With proportion p completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated,

E[r | v] = p·0 + (1-p)·r0 = (1-p) r0

so the population-average per-exposure risk ratio is

RRpe = E[r|v]/r0 = 1-p ,   VEpe = 1-RRpe = p

With constant exposure incidence rate = exposure rate × average per-exposure risk, hence on the marginal population scale

λV = p·0 + (1-p)λ0 = (1-p)λ0 ,   λU = λ0

IRR = λV/λU = 1-p ,   1-IRR = p

constant in time. That is the average reduction in Pr[infection|exposure] across the vaccinated cohort, which is the standard epidemiologic definition of per-exposure VE used with rate studies.

Sv(t)=p+(1-p)Su(t) gives

hV(t)= -d log Sv/dt = λ0 (1-p)Su(t)/[p+(1-p)Su(t)]

* responder, fraction p: per-exposure risk =0, per-exposure VE =1-0/r0 =100%
* non-responder, fraction 1-p: per-exposure risk =r0, per-exposure VE =0%

The marginal 1-IRR=p averages the 100% block in responders with the 0% effect in the 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated fraction and is therefore diluted downwards relative to the 100% per-contact protection seen in responders.

The population-average value p is the correct average reduction across the cohort, but it is a conservative, downward-biased summary of the true per-exposure protection conferred by the vaccine in those who respond.

With a pure all-or-nothing / proportion protected model let p be the fraction completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated with constant force of infection λ0.

Su(t)=exp[-λ0 t], Sv(t)=p+(1-p)Su(t)

h_u=λ0
h_v(t)=-d log Sv/dt = λ0 (1-p)Su(t)/[p+(1-p)Su(t)]

HR(t)=h_v/h_u=(1-p)Su(t)/[p+(1-p)Su(t)] ≤1-p
HR(0)=1-p , HR(t)→0

The instantaneous per-exposure / proportion protected efficacy is
VEe =1-HR(0)=p
and the cumulative risk is proportional
Fv(T)=(1-p)Fu(T), RRcum(T)=1-p, 1-RRcum=p.

The incidence density that is actually reported is events / total calendar person-time

Ev(T)=N(1-p)[1-Su(T)]
PTv(T)=NpT+(1-p)N∫0^T Su(s)ds

IRv(T)=(1-p)[1-Su(T)]/[pT+(1-p)∫0^T Su(s)ds], IRu=λ0

Hence for constant λ0
IRR(T)=(1-p)[1-Su(T)]/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-Su(T)]] <1-p , T>0
1-IRR(T)=pλ0T/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-Su(T)]]>p=1-HR(0)

1-IRR(T)→p as T→0 and 1-IRR(T)→1 as T→∞.

The p completely protected fraction contributes event-free immortal person-time for the whole follow-up while the 1-p susceptible fraction is progressively depleted by infection. The time-averaged hazard is therefore <HR(0)=1-p and the finite follow-up cases per person-time 1-IRR is a person-time diluted upwardly biased proxy for the instantaneous per-exposure reduction p=1-HR(0). The bias grows with follow-up and attack rate.

The unbiased estimator of the all-or-nothing proportion protected is the cumulative risk ratio 1-RRc um=p. For a leaky vaccine HR(t) is constant and 1-IRR=VEe.

On the population-average marginal hazard scale λV=(1-p)λ0 the T→0 limit gives 1-IRR→p and the responder-specific 100 % biological effect is averaged to p on the marginal scale. Under the conventional finite follow-up epidemiologic definition VEe=1-HR(0)=p the observable 1-IRR(T) overestimates it for any realistic T>0, the classic immortal person-time dilution of an all-or-nothing vaccine.

I agree with the Sv(t)=p+(1-p)Su(t) derivation everyone is using and with the resulting expressions for hV(t) and HR(t). The disagreement is really about what estimand the incidence rate ratio is targeting.

hV(t)=λ0(1-p)Su(t)/[p+(1-p)Su(t)] is the hazard conditional on remaining uninfected. It declines because the 1-p phenotypically susceptible stratum is progressively depleted by infection while the p completely protected stratum stays in the risk set and keeps contributing event-free person-time. That is risk-set enrichment / selection in the conditional hazard, not a change in the biological per-exposure susceptibility of an individual who remains susceptible. Conditional on stratum per-exposure risk is constant: 0 in responders, r0 in non-responders.

The IRR used in practice is a marginal population quantity: total events in the vaccinated cohort divided by total person-time accrued by the whole vaccinated cohort, protected person-time included. With constant exposure intensity

E[r|v]=p·0+(1-p)·r0=(1-p)r0

so on the population-average scale

RRpe=E[r|v]/r0=1-p,  VEpe=1-RRpe=p.

Incidence rate = exposure rate × average per-exposure risk, so marginally

λV=p·0+(1-p)λ0=(1-p)λ0, λU=λ0
IRR=λV/λU=1-p, 1-IRR=p

constant in time. That p is the average reduction in Pr[infection|exposure] across the vaccinated population, which is the usual epidemiologic definition of per-exposure VE used with rate studies.

Counting the person-time of the p protected fraction in the denominator is not immortal-person-time bias for a marginal rate; it is the correct denominator for the average rate per vaccinated person. The protected person-time is precisely how the average events per calendar time are reduced to (1-p) of the unvaccinated level. The cumulative risk is coherent with this: Fv(T)=(1-p)Fu(T), RRcum(T)=1-p, 1-RRcum=p.

The 1-IRR(T)>p finite-follow-up calculation is a comparison of a time-averaged conditional hazard with the instantaneous conditional hazard HR(0)=1-p. 1-IRR(T)=pλ0T/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-Su(T)]]>p is the calendar-time average of the declining conditional hazard hV(t) among survivors, not an estimate of the marginal average per-exposure risk. The instantaneous conditional HR(0)=1-p is the per-contact reduction at the moment of first exposure; the marginal rate ratio 1-p is the population-average reduction per exposure averaged over responders and non-responders.

The responder-specific 100% block in the p sub-cohort is a conditional biological effect. The marginal 1-IRR=p is the population average of 100% in the p fraction and 0% in the 1-p fraction, which is the quantity normally reported as V EIRR for an all-or-nothing vaccine. On the conventional population-average definition of per-exposure efficacy, the rate ratio is constant and 1-IRR correctly estimates the average per-exposure efficacy p.

B. underestimate

I agree with the derivations everyone has written for the all-or-nothing model and with the finite-follow-up arithmetic. With p completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated

S_v(t)=p+(1-p)S_0(t)
h_v(t)=λ0 (1-p)S_0(t)/[p+(1-p)S_0(t)]
HR(t)=(1-p)S_0(t)/[p+(1-p)S_0(t)] ≤1-p, HR(0)=1-p, HR(t)↓0

and with events over total calendar person-time

IRR(T)=(1-p)[1-S_0(T)]/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-S_0(T)]]<1-p
1-IRR(T)=pλ0T/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-S_0(T)]]>p

The p fraction does contribute event-free immortal person-time and the 1-p susceptible fraction is progressively depleted, so the calendar-time averaged 1-IRR(T) is indeed >p=1-HR(0) and →1 as T→∞. The overstatement relative to the population-average instantaneous hazard HR(0)=1-p is real.

The question is what we mean by “per-exposure vaccine efficacy”. Mechanistically per-exposure efficacy is the reduction in Pr[infection|exposure] for a host in whom the vaccine can act, i.e. the biological effect per contact.

Conditional on stratum:
* responder, fraction p: per-exposure risk =0, per-exposure VE =1-0/r0 =100%
* non-responder, fraction 1-p: per-exposure risk =r0, per-exposure VE =0%

The marginal incidence rate that enters an IRR is the mixture
λ_V = p·0 + (1-p)λ0 = (1-p)λ_U
so IRR=1-p and 1-IRR=p. That p is the average reduction in incidence per person-time across the whole vaccinated cohort, and it is also the proportion protected 1-RR_cum.

It is not the biological per-exposure reduction realized when the vaccine does act. The marginal 1-IRR=p averages the 100% block in responders with the 0% effect in the 1-p fraction and is therefore diluted downwards relative to the 100% per-contact protection seen in responders. As Colleague 1 himself notes, in responder-specific language 1-IRR is an underestimate of the 100% biological per-exposure effect, with p being the fraction of individuals who experience that effect rather than the per-exposure reduction itself.

The declining conditional hazard h_v(t) is depletion of the at-risk pool, not a change in per-exposure susceptibility for those who remain susceptible. Conditional on remaining susceptible the per-exposure risk stays r0, conditional on being protected it stays 0.

Hence relative to the responder-conditional, per-contact biological definition of per-exposure efficacy, the population-average 1-IRR is a conservative, downward-biased summary of the true per-exposure protection conferred by the vaccine in those who respond. The average reduction per vaccinated person is p, but the per-exposure efficacy in the protected sub-cohort is 100%, which 1-IRR underestimates.

A. overestimate

For a pure all-or-nothing / proportion protected model let p be the fraction completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated with constant force of infection λ0.

$S_u(t)=e^{-\lambda_{0}t},\qquad S_v(t)=p+(1-p)S_u(t)$

$h_u(t)=\lambda_{0}$,
$h_v(t)=-\frac{d}{dt}\log S_v(t)=\lambda_{0}\frac{(1-p)S_u(t)}{p+(1-p)S_u(t)}$

$HR(t)=\frac{h_v}{h_u}=\frac{(1-p)S_u(t)}{p+(1-p)S_u(t)}\le 1-p$, 
$HR(0)=1-p$, $HR(t)\downarrow0$.

The instantaneous per-exposure / proportion protected efficacy is

$VE_e=1-HR(0)=p$

and on the cumulative scale $F_v(T)=(1-p)F_u(T)$, $RR_{cum}(T)=1-p$, $1-RR_{cum}=p$.

The incidence density that is actually reported in practice is events / total person-time.

$E_v(T)=N(1-p)[1-S_u(T)]$,
$PT_v(T)=NpT+(1-p)N\int_0^T S_u(s)ds$,

$IR_v(T)=\frac{(1-p)[1-S_u(T)]}{pT+(1-p)\int_0^T S_u(s)ds},\;IR_u=\lambda_0$

With constant λ0

$IRR(T)=\frac{(1-p)[1-S_u(T)]}{p\lambda_{0}T+(1-p)[1-S_u(T)]}<1-p,\;T>0$

$1-IRR(T)=\frac{p\lambda_{0}T}{p\lambda_{0}T+(1-p)[1-S_u(T)]}>p=1-HR(0)$

$1-IRR(T)\to p$ as $T\to0$ and $1-IRR(T)\to1$ as $T\to\infty$.

The p completely immune fraction contributes event-free immortal person-time for the whole follow-up while the 1-p susceptible fraction is progressively depleted by infection. The calendar-time average hazard therefore falls below $HR(0)=1-p$ and the finite-follow-up cases-per-person-time $1-IRR(T)$ is a person-time diluted upwardly biased proxy for the instantaneous per-exposure reduction $p=1-HR(0)$. The bias grows with follow-up and attack rate.

The unbiased estimator of the all-or-nothing proportion protected is the cumulative risk ratio $1-RR_{cum}=p$. For a leaky vaccine $HR(t)$ is constant and $1-IRR=VE_e$.

The marginal population-average limit $\lambda_V=(1-p)\lambda_0$ gives $1-IRR\to p$ as $T\to0$, and the responder-conditional 100% biological effect is the usual underestimate reading. Under the conventional finite-follow-up epidemiologic definition $VE_e=1-HR(0)=p$, the observable $1$-incidence rate ratio overestimates it for any realistic $T>0$, the classic immortal person-time dilution of an all-or-nothing vaccine.

C. correctly estimate

The vector of disagreement is entirely definitional: what we mean by “per-exposure vaccine efficacy” in an all-or-nothing model.

Let r0 be the per-exposure infection risk in an unvaccinated susceptible host and let exposure intensity be constant in the two arms. With proportion p completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated,

E[r | v] = p·0 + (1-p)·r0 = (1-p) r0

so the population-average per-exposure risk ratio is

RRpe = E[r|v]/r0 = 1-p ,   VEpe = 1-RRpe = p

With constant exposure incidence rate = exposure rate × average per-exposure risk, hence on the marginal population scale

λV = p·0 + (1-p)λ0 = (1-p)λ0 ,   λU = λ0

IRR = λV/λU = 1-p ,   1-IRR = p

constant in time. That is the average reduction in Pr[infection|exposure] across the vaccinated cohort, which is the standard epidemiologic definition of per-exposure VE used with rate studies.

Sv(t)=p+(1-p)Su(t) gives

hV(t)= -d log Sv/dt = λ0 (1-p)Su(t)/[p+(1-p)Su(t)]

which is the hazard conditional on remaining uninfected up to t. It declines from 1-p to 0 because the 1-p susceptible stratum is selectively depleted by infection while the p protected stratum stays in the risk set and continues to contribute event-free person-time. That is risk-set enrichment / selection in the conditional hazard, not a change in the biological per-exposure susceptibility of an individual who remains susceptible. Conditional on stratum, per-exposure risk is constant: 0 in responders, r0 in non-responders.

Counting the person-time contributed by the p protected fraction in the denominator of the incidence rate is not a bias for a marginal rate; it is the correct denominator for the average rate per vaccinated person. The protected person-time is precisely how the average events per calendar time are reduced to (1-p) of the unvaccinated level. The cumulative risk is coherent with this: Fv(T)=(1-p)Fu(T), RRcum(T)=1-p, 1-RRcum=p.

The 1-IRR(T)=pλ0T/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-Su(T)]]>p and 1-IRR(T)→1 as T→∞ that is quoted for A is the time-averaged conditional hazard among survivors compared with the instantaneous conditional hazard HR(0)=1-p. It is a comparison of a conditional-on-survival quantity with an integrated average hazard. Under the conventional population-average definition of per-exposure efficacy, the marginal incidence density ratio recovers the average per-exposure reduction p without bias for an all-or-nothing vaccine. The responder-specific 100% block in the p sub-cohort averages with 0% in the 1-p fraction to the population mean p that IRR reports, which is the quantity normally reported as VEIRR.

Hence on the standard definition, 1-IRR correctly estimates the population-average per-exposure vaccine efficacy = p.

C. correctly estimate

The disagreement here is not the algebra, it's what estimand the incidence rate ratio is trying to recover.

$S_v(t)=p+(1-p)S_u(t)$ is correct, and
$h_v(t)=-\frac{d}{dt}\log S_v(t)=\lambda_0\frac{(1-p)S_u(t)}{p+(1-p)S_u(t)}$
is the hazard conditional on being in the risk set and remaining uninfected up to time t. It declines because the $1-p$ phenotypically susceptible stratum is selectively depleted by infection while the $p$ completely protected stratum stays in the denominator and continues to contribute event-free person-time. That is risk-set enrichment / selection in a conditional hazard, not a change in the biological per-exposure susceptibility of an individual who remains susceptible. Conditional on stratum, per-exposure risk is constant: 0 in responders, $r_0$ in non-responders.

An incidence rate ratio is a marginal population quantity: total events in the vaccinated cohort divided by total person-time accrued by the whole vaccinated cohort, protected person-time included. With constant exposure intensity,

$E[r\mid v]=p\cdot0+(1-p)\cdot r_0=(1-p)r_0$,

so on the population-average scale

$RR_{pe}=E[r\mid v]/r_0=1-p$, $\quad VE_{pe}=1-RR_{pe}=p$.

Incidence rate = exposure rate $\times$ average per-exposure risk, so at the marginal level

$\lambda_V=p\cdot0+(1-p)\lambda_0=(1-p)\lambda_0$, $\quad \lambda_U=\lambda_0$,

$IRR=\lambda_V/\lambda_U=1-p$, $1-IRR=p$,

constant in time. That $p$ is the average reduction in Pr[infection|exposure] across the vaccinated population, which is the standard epidemiologic definition of per-exposure vaccine efficacy used in rate studies.

Counting the person-time of the $p$ protected fraction in the denominator is not immortal-person-time bias for a marginal rate; it is the correct denominator for the average rate per vaccinated person. The protected person-time is precisely how the average events per calendar time are reduced to $(1-p)$ of the unvaccinated level. The coherence with the cumulative scale is $F_v(T)=(1-p)F_u(T)$, $RR_{cum}(T)=1-p$, $1-RR_{cum}=p$.

The $1-IRR(T)>p$ calculation that is quoted is a comparison of a finite-follow-up time-averaged conditional hazard with the instantaneous conditional hazard $HR(0)=1-p$. $1-HR(0)=p$ is the instantaneous conditional hazard ratio at time zero, the proportion protected at first exposure. The finite follow-up average $1-IRR(T)=\frac{p\lambda_0T}{p\lambda_0T+(1-p)[1-S_u(T)]}>p$ and $1-IRR(T)\to1$ as $T\to\infty$ are calendar-time artefacts of depletion of the at-risk pool in the conditional hazard among survivors. They do not change the marginal average per-exposure risk $E[r\mid v]=(1-p)r_0$.

On the conventional population-average definition of per-exposure VE, the marginal incidence density ratio recovers the average per-exposure reduction without bias for an all-or-nothing vaccine, and $1-IRR=p$ correctly estimates the average per-exposure efficacy. The responder-specific 100% block in the $p$ sub-cohort averages with 0% in the $1-p$ fraction to the population mean $p$ that IRR reports, which is the quantity normally reported as $VE_{IRR}$ for an all-or-nothing vaccine.

A. overestimate

For a pure all-or-nothing / proportion protected model let p be the fraction completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated with unvaccinated force of infection λ0.

$S_{u}(t)=e^{-\lambda_{0}t},\qquad S_{v}(t)=p+(1-p)S_{u}(t)$

$h_{u}(t)=\lambda_{0},\qquad 
h_{v}(t)=-\frac{d}{dt}\log S_{v}(t)=\lambda_{0}\frac{(1-p)S_{u}(t)}{p+(1-p)S_{u}(t)}$

$HR(t)=\frac{h_{v}}{h_{u}}=\frac{(1-p)S_{u}(t)}{p+(1-p)S_{u}(t)}\le 1-p$,
$HR(0)=1-p$, $HR(t)\downarrow0$.

The instantaneous / per-exposure, proportion protected efficacy is

$VE_{e}=1-HR(0)=p$

and on the cumulative scale

$F_{v}(T)=(1-p)F_{u}(T)$, $RR_{cum}(T)=1-p$, $1-RR_{cum}=p$.

The incidence density actually reported from a finite follow-up is cases per total calendar person-time

$E_{v}(T)=N(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]$
$PT_{v}(T)=NpT+(1-p)N\int_{0}^{T}S_{u}(s)ds$

$IR_{v}(T)=\frac{(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}{pT+(1-p)\int_{0}^{T}S_{u}(s)ds}$, $IR_{u}=\lambda_{0}$

Hence with constant λ0

$IRR(T)=\frac{(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}{p\lambda_{0}T+(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}<1-p$, $T>0$

$1-IRR(T)=\frac{p\lambda_{0}T}{p\lambda_{0}T+(1-p)[1-S_{u}(T)]}>p=1-HR(0)$

$1-IRR(T)\to p$ as $T\to0$ and $1-IRR(T)\to1$ as $T\to\infty$.

The p completely immune fraction contributes event-free person-time for the whole follow-up while the 1-p susceptible fraction is progressively depleted by infection. The calendar-time average hazard therefore falls below $HR(0)=1-p$ and the finite-follow-up cases-per-person-time $1-IRR(T)$ is a person-time diluted, upwardly biased proxy for the instantaneous per-exposure reduction $p=1-HR(0)$. The bias grows with follow-up and attack rate.

The unbiased estimator of the all-or-nothing proportion protected is the cumulative risk ratio $1-RR_{cum}=p$. For a leaky vaccine $HR(t)$ is constant and $1-IRR=VE_{e}$. Under the conventional finite-follow-up epidemiologic definition $VE_{e}=1-HR(0)=p$ the observable $1-IRR(T)$ overestimates it, the classic immortal-person-time dilution of an all-or-nothing vaccine.

C. correctly estimate

The disagreement is entirely about which estimand we call “per-exposure vaccine efficacy”. 

With an all-or-nothing mechanism let the per-exposure risk in an unvaccinated susceptible be r0 and let exposure intensity be the same in the two arms. In the vaccinated cohort the average per-exposure risk is the mixture

E[r|v] = p·0 + (1-p)·r0 = (1-p) r0

so on the population-average scale

RR_pe = E[r|v]/r0 = 1-p ,  VE_pe = 1-RR_pe = p.

Incidence rate = exposure rate × average per-exposure risk. On the marginal level

λV = p·0 + (1-p)·λ0 = (1-p)λ0 ,   λU = λ0

so

IRR = λV/λU = 1-p ,   1-IRR = p

constant in time under constant exposure intensity. The cumulative risk is coherent with this:

Sv(t)=p+(1-p)Su(t) ⇒ Fv(T)=(1-p)Fu(T) ⇒ RRcum(T)=1-p , 1-RRcum=p.

hV(t)= -d log Sv/dt = λ0 (1-p)Su(t)/[p+(1-p)Su(t)] is the hazard conditional on remaining uninfected up to t. It declines from 1-p to 0 because the 1-p phenotypically susceptible stratum is selectively depleted by infection while the p completely protected stratum stays in the risk set and continues to contribute event-free person-time. That is risk-set enrichment / selection in the conditional hazard, not a change in the biological per-exposure susceptibility of an individual who remains susceptible. Conditional on stratum, per-exposure risk is constant: 0 in responders, r0 in non-responders.

Counting the person-time of the p protected fraction in the denominator of the incidence rate is not immortal-person-time bias for the marginal rate; it is the correct denominator for the average rate per vaccinated person. The protected person-time is precisely how the average events per calendar time are reduced to (1-p) of the unvaccinated level. The finite follow-up expression

1-IRR(T)= pλ0T/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-Su(T)]] > p

is a comparison of a time-averaged conditional hazard among survivors with the instantaneous conditional hazard HR(0)=1-p. It is the calendar-time average of hV(t) compared with HR(0). The 1-IRR(T)→1 as T→∞ is the familiar depletion-of-the-at-risk-pool artefact of a conditional hazard, not a change in average per-exposure risk per se.

On the conventional epidemiologic definition of per-exposure VE as the average reduction in Pr[infection|exposure] across the vaccinated population, the marginal incidence density ratio recovers that average and 1-IRR = p correctly estimates the population-average per-exposure efficacy. The responder-specific 100% block in the p sub-cohort is a conditional biological effect; the marginal 1-IRR = p is the population average of 100% in the p fraction and 0% in the 1-p fraction, which is the quantity normally reported as VEIRR for an all-or-nothing vaccine.

* Overestimate camp — A. Finite-follow-up 1-IRR(T)>p=1-HR(0). Time-averaged 1-IRR(T)>p for any realistic T, so rate-based VE upwardly biases true per-exposure / proportion-protected efficacy. Unbiased estimator is cumulative risk ratio 1-RR=p. Held by colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7. They stress immortal person-time dilution, risk-set enrichment, HR(t)↓0, bias grows with follow-up and attack rate; for leaky vaccine HR constant so 1-IRR=VEper-exposure.

* Correctly estimate camp — C. Per-exposure efficacy defined as population-average reduction in risk per exposure. Marginal average hazard λV=p·0+(1-p)λ0=(1-p)λ0, so IRR=1-p and 1-IRR=p on marginal average scale. With constant exposure intensity incidence rate = exposure×average per-exposure risk, so rate ratio correctly recovers population mean per-exposure effect. The all-or-nothing / proportion protected model with p completely protected and 1-p phenotypically unvaccinated, λ0 constant, gives

Su(t)=exp[-λ0 t], Sv(t)=p+(1-p)Su(t)
hu=λ0, hv(t)=λ0 (1-p)Su(t)/[p+(1-p)Su(t)]
HR(t)= (1-p)Su(t)/[p+(1-p)Su(t)] ≤1-p, HR(0)=1-p, HR(t)→0

Cumulative risk is proportional: Fv(T)=(1-p)Fu(T), RRcum=1-p, 1-RRcum=p.
Instantaneous / per-exposure proportion protected efficacy on the conditional hazard scale is VEe=1-HR(0)=p.

Incidence density using total calendar person-time:
Ev(T)=N(1-p)[1-Su(T)], PTv(T)=NpT+(1-p)N∫0^T Su(s)ds
IRv(T)=(1-p)[1-Su(T)]/[pT+(1-p)∫0^T Su(s)ds], IRu=λ0
IRR(T)=(1-p)[1-Su(T)]/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-Su(T)]] <1-p  for T>0
1-IRR(T)=pλ0T/[pλ0T+(1-p)[1-Su(T)]]>p=1-HR(0)
1-IRR(T)→p as T→0 and →1 as T→∞. Bias grows with follow-up and attack rate.

The p fraction contributes event-free immortal person-time while the 1-p susceptible fraction is progressively depleted, so the calendar-time averaged hazard < HR(0). The cumulative risk ratio 1-RRc um=p is unbiased for the proportion protected.

Round 4 majority: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6,7 give the same derivation and conclude A. overestimate. They state under the conventional finite-follow-up epidemiologic definition VEe=1-HR(0)=p, the observable 1-IRR(T) overestimates it for any realistic T>0, with bias vanishing only as T→0. For a leaky vaccine HR(t) is constant and 1-IRR=VEe.

Correctly estimate camp: Colleagues 5,8,9,14 argue the IRR is a marginal population quantity. Marginal per-exposure risk E[r|v]=p·0+(1-p)r0=(1-p)r0, so λV=(1-p)λ0, IRR=1-p, 1-IRR=p constant in time. hv(t) decline is risk-set enrichment / depletion in the conditional hazard, not a change in per-exposure susceptibility conditional on stratum. On the population-average marginal definition of per-exposure VE as average reduction in Pr[infection|exposure] across the vaccinated cohort, 1-IRR correctly estimates p.

Underestimate camp: Colleagues 2,13 stress responder-specific biological definition. Conditional on being a responder per-exposure VE=100%, conditional on non-responder 0%. Marginal 1-IRR=p averages 100% and 0% and is therefore a downward-biased summary of the 100% biological per-exposure effect realized in the p sub-cohort.

Unresolved is which definition the question intends. The rigorous finite-time derivations in rounds 2-4 converge on A overestimate for VEe=1-HR(0)=p. The C position is definition-dependent using the marginal population mean hazard and ignoring depletion; the B position is definition-dependent using the conditional 100% biological effect in responders. Majority of detailed derivations in round 4 continue to point to A overestimate with the immortal-person-time dilution, while noting the definitional variants.
